Mubarak and Progress confirmed the following instructions if the driver is blocked due to Criminal Record Check):

*Tier 1 instructions:*

* Go to the driver’s profile > _Documents_ tab and click _View_ for the Huru background check
* Check the _Outcome_ on the document_:_
** *Positive:* Inform the driver that we can’t unblock their account
** *Clear* or *negative*: Escalate the case to Tier 2

*Tier 2 instructions:*

*Step 1: Verify the driver document authenticity*

* Verify the authenticity of the Huru report:
** *Local drivers:*
*** Go to [+Huru+|https://portal.huru.co.za/verify]
*** Fill out the required fields based on the information on the Huru report on the driver’s profile:
**** _Supplier reference_ and _Reference_ can be found in the _Detailed Verification Results_ report section)
**** _Identifier_ is the driver’s personal code
** *Foreign drivers:*
*** Go to [+Afiswitch+|https://www.afiswitch.co.za/Default.aspx]
*** In _Result Authentication,_ fill out the fields based on the information on the driver’s document
*** If the search returns the same document, it’s an authentic document
* Verify the Dekra report:
** Log into the [+Dekra smart+|https://rsa.dekrasmart.com/Analysis/Agendamento/ListaAgendamento] website
** Change _Type_ to _Unit#_
** Select _Product_ as _Shuttle vehicle inspection_
** Select _Status_ as _Completed_
** Set an appropriate date range for the inspection report
** In _Value_, enter the vehicle registration number

*Step 2: Proceed based on verification results*

* If the authenticity of documents was verified:
** Unblock the driver
** Inform them about the unblocking
* If you couldn’t verify the documents' authenticity, inform the driver about the following:
** The outcome of their Huru criminal record check and Dekra inspection
** We’re unable to unblock them
** If they didn’t pass the Huru check, inform the driver that they need a police clearance and to go through the expungement process to get their record cleared if they qualify

{code:python}import pandas as pd
import os

# Replace 'filename.csv' with the actual name of your CSV file
file_path = '/Users/carloscasio/Downloads/cash_file.csv'

# Create a new directory for storing the separate CSV files
output_directory = '/Users/carloscasio/Downloads/Files'
os.makedirs(output_directory, exist_ok=True)

# Read the CSV file into a DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Convert the 'date' column to a datetime type
df['Balance Entry Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Balance Entry Date'])

# Set the start and end dates for filtering
start_date = pd.to_datetime('2022-01-22')
end_date = pd.to_datetime('2023-06-06')

# Create a loop for each date
for date in pd.date_range(start_date, end_date, freq='D'):
    # Filter the rows for the current date
    filtered_df = df[df['Balance Entry Date'] == date]
    
    # Generate the output file path
    output_date = date + pd.DateOffset(days=1)
    output_file = os.path.join(output_directory, f'{output_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")}.csv')
    
    # Save the filtered DataFrame as a separate CSV file
    filtered_df.to_csv(output_file, index=False){code}

# You need to change the path where you save the csv file to read, or if it’s in Downloads, at least change the username

### Terms for BC referral from the garages attached 
## It is unlikely drivers would be asked to wear a shirt/ branding - we would ask they wear their green badge (which they receive for being a taxi driver) - to show to other drivers they are also one. Unlikely to be specific KPIs to meet, we would start using ambassadors on a trial basis, with an hourly/ daily rate and/or reward per referral. So 1) we need to determine what was actually agreed when signing the contract as that will determine how the wording of the contract shall be interpreted and 2) if no aim between the parties can be determined other than the actual wording of the contract then we can interpret it solely based on the words. 

In the event of number 2 above, the contract and these terms must then be interpreted as having the effect that in case of damage to the vehicle, when it is returned by you to the Det Grønne Autohus A/S, you must pay a deductible of DKK 5,000 and that this deductible amount only must be paid +*one time*+ irrespective of whether there is several or even many specific damages to the vehicle. Apart from paying the deductible amount, you will be covered under the contract as though the vehicle is covered by an all-risk property insurance (“kaskoforsikring”) irrespective of whether the vehicle is or is not covered by such an insurance. This means that you shall not pay for the costs of the damages to the extent they are greater (higher) than DKK 5,000 (unless one or more of the damages are caused by you intentionally or by gross negligence). 

This assessment is based on the following clauses in the contract: 

----

*Forsikring*

Ansvarsforsikring: -

Kaskoforsikring: -

Selvrisiko inkl. moms: {color:#ff5630}5.000{color}

* {color:#ff5630}Lejer hæfter for alle skader, som ikke er eller ville være dækket af en tegnet{color}

{color:#ff5630}kaskoforsikring.{color}

uvedkommende.

*Lejer godkender opgørelsen*

[…]

Selvrisikodækning {color:#ff5630}5.000,00{color}

----

We should then go back to the lessor and 1) put this view forward as soon as possible and not pay the invoice unless this matter has been settled; 2) If they refuse to lower the amount, we should still aim to find a settlement with the lessor as legal proceedings will cost us a lot more than paying the full amount of the claimed damages. Briefly checked google on possible solutions:

* NPM doesn’t able to return list of packages from registry 
* Jfrog provides some black-box tool to migrate from nexus to jfrog, but it also copy repositories what exist in nexus, so not an option due to we use configuration via TF 
* Found one old tool to do it, but it’s quite outdated
* Nexus API don’t let to get full list of packages
* Nexus has HTML representation for NPM repository 

Based on it, decided to create a simple bash script to backfill artifacts from nexus to jfrog once.
I have also tested this on the latest develop branch, and the modal/list is requested only once, marking this issue rejected.
Not reproducible on latest develop branch.

{noformat}#!/bin/bash
##Instruction:
#1. Run docker with nodejs: docker run -it -d node
#2. Copy script in container
#3. Execute script with npm command as arg ./npm_to_jfrog.sh pack
#4. Wait until script will finish
#6. Make publish of downloaded tarball by comman ./npm_to_jfrog.sh publish.
#7. Wait until script will finish
#8. Done

start=$(date +%s)

npm_command=$1

function download_packages {

  #Update /etc/hosts in docker direct sed doesn't work to IP of nexus
  cat /etc/hosts | sed -E '/.*npm.internal.*/d' > tmp_hosts
  echo 172.28.49.127 npm.internal >> tmp_hosts
  cp tmp_hosts /etc/hosts
  rm tmp_hosts

  repo_name=npm_upload

  repositories=`curl -s  https://nexus.boltint.net/service/rest/repository/browse/$repo_name/ | grep -v "Parent Directory" | grep "<a href" | awk -F ">" '{print $3}'  | sed 's/<\/a//g'`

  packages_counter=0
  for dir in $repositories ; do
     if [[ $dir != *"tgz"* ]]; then
       packages=`curl -s  https://nexus.boltint.net/service/rest/repository/browse/$repo_name/$dir/ | grep -v "Parent Directory" | grep -v "zed" | grep "<a href" | awk -F ">" '{print $3}'  | sed 's/<\/a//g'`
       for sub_repo in $packages ; do
          if [[ $sub_repo !=  *"tgz"* ]]; then
             sub_sub_repo=`curl -s  https://nexus.boltint.net/service/rest/repository/browse/$repo_name/$dir/$sub_repo/ | grep -v "Parent Directory" | grep -v "zed" | grep "<a href" | awk -F ">" '{print $3}'  | sed 's/<\/a//g'`
             for sub_packages in $sub_sub_repo; do
               npm_package=`echo $dir/$sub_packages |  sed -E 's/-([0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+.*).tgz/@\1/g'`
               #npm $npm_command $npm_package --registry http://npm.internal:4873
               ((packages_counter=packages_counter+1))
               echo Downloaded $packages_counter of 811
             done
          else
             npm_package=`echo $sub_repo |  sed -E 's/-([0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+.*).tgz/@\1/g'`

              ((packages_counter=packages_counter+1))
              echo Downloaded $packages_counter of 811
              #npm $npm_command $npm_package --registry http://npm.internal:4873
          fi
       done
     fi
  done
}

function publish_packages {
  packages_counter=0
  #Update /etc/hosts in docker direct sed doesn't work to IP of jfrog
  cat /etc/hosts | sed -E '/.*npm.internal.*/d' > tmp_hosts
  echo 172.28.102.26 npm.internal >> tmp_hosts
  cp tmp_hosts /etc/hosts
  rm tmp_hosts

  cat >/root/.npmrc <<EOL
registry=http://npm.internal:4873/
//npm.internal:4873/:_authToken=XXXXXXXX
EOL
  for tarball in `ls *tgz`; do
     npm $npm_command $tarball --registry http://npm.internal:4873
     ((packages_counter=packages_counter+1))
     echo Published $packages_counter of 811
  done
}


if [[ $npm_command == *"pack"* ]]; then
  echo STARTING DOWNLOAD OF PACKAGES FROM NEXUS
  download_packages

elif [[ $npm_command == *"publish"* ]]; then
  echo PUBLISH TARBALLS INTO JFROG
  publish_packages
fi

end=$(date +%s)
echo "Execution time: $(($end-$start)) seconds"{noformat}
2QA: *Fill in your notes to the QA team*

So we have 811 npm packages in Nexus, copied them as a tarball on publish to jfrog. 

Some numbers:

* Execution time: 1996 seconds - to get all tarballs ~33 minutes, so may be run again if needed (or even possibly optimise the script to make it in parallel, but doesn’t worth it. 
* Size of tarballs: du -sh = 3.5G . 
* Publish slightly slower, but because of more heavy procedure.



Also, if re-run script, not issue so far, in case of download just will download again.

In case of upload, it just will return an error that package exist and will continue to upload next one.

In the case of a composite index with a combination of a number and a string column, the determination of the gap for gap locking purposes is based on the comparison rules of the number column.

When a composite index has a number column followed by a string column, the gap locking behavior depends on the comparison rules for numeric values.

The determination of the gap between index records is performed by comparing the values of the composite index columns based on their numeric properties. In this case, the numeric comparison rules are used to determine the gap.

For example, let's consider a composite index on columns {{column1}} (number) and {{column2}} (string). The gap locking behavior would be as follows:

# If the numeric values being processed in the query are within an existing range of index records, the gap lock is acquired between the existing records based on the comparison of the numeric values.
# If the numeric values fall outside the existing range, the gap lock is acquired at the beginning or end of the index range based on the numeric comparison.

It's important to note that the comparison rules for numeric values typically follow the standard numerical ordering, such as comparing values based on magnitude (greater than, less than) or equality.

The gap determination in the case of a number + string composite index relies on the comparison rules for the numeric column. The specific behavior may also depend on the data type and storage format of the numeric column.

So, the data is stored in two file formats: raw CSV (100% raw from the PSP report portal), and a file format to load the data into our data analytics platform. The files are stored in a S3 bucket, and currently only our team has access to read the bucket. However, the table is also published as a database in the data analytics platform, and connected to Looker. People with generic Looker access couldn’t access the table, but those who have access to Commerce’s Looker instance could. 

We’re aware of this risk, and currently it is not 100% necessary for the Commerce’s Looker instance to access the database schema. So, we’re working on migrating some tables and will restrict the access to the database once all relevant tables are migrated. So, in the near future, only Finance DWH engineer and Payments analysts are able to access the data. 

As for the necessity, as far as I’m aware of, these PIIs are not necessary for any reporting purposes. However, we want to retain all reports from PSP for data retention purpose, as PSPs only publish the report for a limited period of time and will remove the report from their server after a limited period of time. We still don’t know what’s the use case of this data retention, either for audit/other compliance purposes, though.

Hey Anna,

We do not separately invoice outstanding amount charges because technically this is a sum that was already included in the previous order’s invoice, but not charged. So, the invoice of the order where this outstanding sum is coming from + the order where this outsanding sum was charged alongside the ride fare adds up to the total of these 2 trips. They can use the invoices for these 2 trips. 

To examplify:

* Order 1: 
** Ride fare: 10€
** Charged: 7€
** Outstanding: 3€
** Invoice: 10€
* Order 2:
** Ride fare: 15€
** Charged: 18€
** Outstanding: 0€
** Invoice: 15€

Invoice Total: 10+15=25, Charged total 7+18=25.

Hey team,

As of the 1st of March, we have switched to “netted” (simplified) commission invoicing in Latvia. That means that all bonuses/compensations/campaigns of the driver are reduced from their commission (so they pay less commission). In addition to that, rider discounts are also deducted from their commission. That’s because during the ride they basically compensate the rider for their discounts.

So, at the end of the day the calculation is:

Monthly commission - campaigns or bonuses or compensations - rider discounts = total commission invoice

Relevant notification for this change in Terms and Conditions was sent to drivers on the 15th/16th of February.

🇪🇪 In Estonia, it will work this way:

* CS Safety receives the report, does not place any block, creates a tool, and closes as CBC;
* CS Safety handles reporting party tickets;
* Local Ops get a “Vehicle Block Bot” notification in this channel;
* Local Ops block the vehicle and follow up with the fleet owner (if needed);
* Local Ops reacts to the “Vehicle Block Bot” notification in the channel indicating the notification has been reviewed and actioned (adding a comment in the thread with any actions taken).

----

In 🇵🇹 Portugal, the process is very similar to the Estonian one (no driver blocks), but CS still contacts the driver and asks for the vehicle pictures. 

----

I am working on trying to align also the 🇩🇪 German process to make it as similar as possible (considering market specifics) to have some sort of standard approach. Atm the German process still requires Driver Investigative blocks while waiting for pictures.

----

Hi Ewa,  
 
 Thank you very much.   
 
 Just a note from my side that the employer field is missing on the agreements and please make sure that the agreements will be corrected and signed and then uploaded again.  
 Re your query (it refers only to Bolt Rides only (at least for now)), the payroll provider's software is built in a way that the vendor needs to upload the agreement in order to calculate the salary and tax reliefs. The tax reliefs can be calculated only once a month. Because we make a payout in July, the software is able to calculate the tax relief only if the extension of the contract for July is uploaded because this is July's tax relief which can decrease the tax from June's payroll paid in July. For tax purposes June's payroll paid in July is considered as July payroll. So in case of mid month extensions for Bolt Rides we have to receive the agreement 1 month prior in order to calculate the tax reliefs correctly.

I believe that it is absolutely necessary that we implement this change (for orders over 40eur) just overall for all NOT DELIVERED orders. Agents must contact both the provider and the courier to verify the status of the order, even if it has already been marked as delivered. This crucial step is necessary to prevent unnecessary refunds to BB (our double, since some ask for a refund to CC, when the refund is issued to BB). I have done a deep-dive and nearly 20% of all manual refunds in Latvia are a result of orders being reported as undelivered, including those that were eventually delivered. This is an alarming figure that we cannot ignore. It is crucial that agents are aware of their responsibility to contact all relevant parties and confirm the delivery status for orders exceeding 40EUR. This applies to both Lithuania (LT) and Latvia (LV). While I understand that implementing this change globally may pose challenges, I firmly believe it will result in cost savings and an enhanced user experience. By double-checking with providers and couriers through direct phone calls, we can avoid issuing refunds too hastily, particularly for orders with a refund value exceeding 40EUR. So all we need is to make sure agents call both parties without issuing a full refund for not delivered orders (over 40eur). It would just be a sentence in Eater did not receive the order

Mubarak reported that there are no instructions in the KB for when drivers have payouts disabled in Admin and they reach out asking why they’re not receiving their payouts.

I’ve confirmed the new instructions to add to the KB article 🚗 [Driver did not receive payout|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360012567634]:

* Add the following steps in *Step 1* (as the first steps in this step group):
** On the driver profile > _Account information,_ check if the _Payout disabled_ checkbox is ticked
*** If it’s ticked, go to the section _Driver payouts are disabled_
* Create a new section *Driver payouts are disabled* with the following steps:
** On the driver’s profile > _Change log_ tab, find the log entry with *is_payout_disabled*
** Check who disabled the payouts
** Check what was the reason and follow further instructions:
*** *_Fraud_* or *_Not valid TIN:_* Escalate the case to the local OPS team
*** *_Not valid payment details:_* Inform the driver that their payment details are invalid and follow the CS process [Driver requests changing banking details|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013903520]
*** *_Partner request:_* Enable the payouts
*** If *_Other_**, or the* *reason wasn't provided*: Contact the person who disabled the payouts to confirm if the payouts can be enabled
** If driver payouts could be enabled:
*** Enable them (if not done already)
*** Inform the driver about it
** If driver payouts can’t be enabled, inform the driver about it

* Manual adjustment from the first courier’s mistake kicked in and courier received $0, not $63
* Eater’s balance now became minus $63 from the first order 
* On top of that, he didn’t pay for the second order either because the positive balance there is wrong - hence another $63 negative balance is added 
* $63 + $63 = $126

Upstream clusters handled as with no traffic if {{upstream_cx_total}} metric is not  collected.
In such case health check interval will be 10 minutes instead of 4s.

The workaround is to add {{- suffix: upstream_cx_total}} into our Envoy config.
The [doc|https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/core/v3/health_check.proto] contains nothing about this.

{noformat}no_traffic_interval
(Duration) The "no traffic interval" is a special health check interval that is used when a cluster has never had traffic routed to it.
This lower interval allows cluster information to be kept up to date, without sending a potentially large amount of active health checking traffic for no reason. 
Once a cluster has been used for traffic routing, Envoy will shift back to using the standard health check interval that is defined. 
Note that this interval takes precedence over any other.

The default value for "no traffic interval" is 60 seconds.{noformat}

Just to clarify how to read the report:

* City filter → to filter out city(/cities) you want to check
* Local Date filter → to specify the timeframe, by default it’s {{is any time}} meaning since the beginning of operations (in UA)
* To Agent Type → this needs to be {{delivery_courier}} as we're checking bag deposits to the couriers
* Total Orders filter → to filter out the total orders (both cancelled & completed) done by the courier
* Delivery Bag Deposit Count filter → how many times the bag deposit has been added to the courier
* Delivery Bag Deposit Return Count filter → how many times the return of bag deposit has been added to the courier

So to check the couriers who haven’t “interacted” with adjustment type “delivery_bag_deposit” simply use the filter

{{Delivery Bag Deposit Count  = 0}}

To come back to the toll abuse. As i mentioned, we at fraud can’t control the polygons and whether the driver trigger the fee. What we could do is look for the drivers that over do it. I ran some quick numbers to get the following drivers that hit the velocity of over doing it. We still can’t have 100% confidence that this is abuse, because it is assumed that if they hit the polygon they went to the toll. The first layer pulls order where drivers have more than 5 orders where the tolls make up more that 50% of the final price. Main edits that we’d like to highlight are: 

*Invoicing & Payment*

* we added prior written notice requirement with no less than 30d in case of suspension of the service because based on the principle of reasonableness, at least 30 days' notice must be given before the termination of cooperation. The parties can always terminate earlier by mutual agreement;

* deleted late charge wording, which would allow to impose late charges upon Bolt within 10d from the due date, because it is not in accordance with the principle of good contracts and the imposition of liquidated damages with such short notice is against our internal rules. We will not default on invoices that have been properly prepared, sent to the correct channel and submitted under contract.

*Assignment*

* we have deleted Rocket Lab’s unfettered right to assign this OI to other persons as this is contrary to our internal policy. We have added a wording that any assignment can be done only on our prior written consent.  

*Billing dispute*

* we have added a specification that any billing dispute can be submitted within 10 

*business* days, as 10 days may in some cases include weekends and public holidays and thus leave us too little time to reach.

*IP & Data Protection and Confidentiality and Publicity*

* we have added additional wording to safeguard IP and personal data (should it be shared) and added direct reference to Bolt Brand Guidelines.

*Limitation of Liability*

* reworded the clause to be mutually binding.

*Term*

* excluded auto-renewals, as we cannot accept auto-renewals in Bolt.  

*Termination*

* we have aligned the wording with one made under Invoicing & Payment whereby parties may terminate the OI with 30d advance notification. This leaves both parties enough time to make any necessary technical and organisational preparations necessary in case of termination. The parties can always terminate earlier by mutual agreement.

*Governing law and Jurisdiction*

* proposing Spanish law and Spanish courts. Both companies are European, this it does not make sense to agree upon Uruguay law and jurisdiction. Furthermore, Bolt cannot accept law and jurisdiction of a country where it does not operate nor have an active registered entity.

There are 2 main principles to follow:

*Daily rest time* (according to which the employee must have at least 11 consecutive hours of rest time in a 24-hour period (i.e. the employee can work a maximum of 13 hours with overtime in one work shift).

*Weekly rest period*, according to which the employee must be able to rest for at least 48 consecutive hours in the case of normal working time calculation, or at least 36 consecutive hours in the case of cumulative working time calculation.

The daily rest period is not part of the weekly rest period, but must precede the weekly rest period. This means that the employee must be guaranteed consecutive daily and weekly rest at least once in seven days: 11 hours + 36 or 48 hours = a total of 47 or 59 hours. Until now, the working and rest time requirements have been considered fulfilled if the employee receives a weekly rest period of 36 or 48 hours once in seven days without being preceded by a daily rest period of 11 hours.

*Example:* According to the current practice, if an employee with a schedule ended the working day on Friday at 20:00 and was given weekly rest time, the employee could start a new working day at 8:00 on Sunday morning (that is, after 36 hours). From now on, the weekly rest period must be preceded by a daily rest period, so the employee could start the working day at the earliest on Sunday at 19:00 (or after 47 hours).

The issue in the last two cases (fleet_id: 31266,37503):

In the old system, the compensations are stored per {{uid+uid_type}} in the {{compensation_import_items}} table, and the {{date}} filed is [only set on insert|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/ca8db88469673e5aebda5087763c1548dc97657f/src/platform/commerce/invoicing/main/import/table/CompensationImportItemTable.ts#L15-L38], therefore when a compensation with the {{uid+uid_type}} is updated in the following days, the date won't change and no new {{compensation}} record generated, compared to the {{RHB}} system where a new record is generated for every update. Because of this, in the {{invoicing}} systems, the number of compensation records can be less than in the {{ride_hailing_billing}} system. As I can see in these cases the num of records varies, but the end result is the same (sum of the records).

The first case seems to be different because there the {{RHB}} system returned an empty list. I'll continue investigating that issue.

Date: 4 July 2023 

Start time: 14:37 

Time engaged: 33 minutes

Present: AB, AK, Mediator

+*SUMMARY OF CALL*+

The mediation telephone conference took place this afternoon at 14:37 and lasted a total of 33 minutes. 

The claimant is not budging on his position and he asserted to the mediator that Bolt admitted liability (which we did not, we acknowledged his safety concern), he has also asserted that there were delays in responding to him. I defended all the arguments raised, reiterated the timeline and sequence of events to the mediator. I also informed the mediator that the claimant has refused to provide any evidence (the video), has not quantified his costs, has failed to adhere to the Pre Action Protocol and the Civil Procedure Rules and has also emailed me personally making threats that he will report me to the financial ombudsman. The claimant continued to maintain his position that we ‘admitted liability’ and ignored him for days. I informed the mediator once court proceedings were issued we stopped engaging with the claimant, however responded to all court requests, the mediator understood why we stopped engaging. 

Following a call with Josh yesterday, it was decided that the initial offering would be a full refund of the trip and a £20 goodwill gesture credit to the account, this was put to the claimant, he refused. We put the upper limit offer of full refund of the trip and a £50 goodwill gesture credit to the account, this offer was also refused. The mediator informed us that the claimant is seeking the amount he claimed on the particulars. We asked for clarify of how this sum has been quantified as it bears no correlation to the trip price (£20.30), the mediator informed us that this is how the claimant has quantified the amount: 

£20 trip fare

£35 court fee 

£150 stress and distress fee for not responding to him 

£100 to be given to a mental health charity 

We asked if the claimant was willing to settle today and the mediator said it was a hard no, the claimant won't accept anything less than what he has requested. The mediator informed us that the next steps are: 

* Bolt will receive a notice of transfer, we should follow the courts directions
* Bolt will be provided with a hearing notice
* The court will request all evidence from both parties 
* The matter will be listed for a hearing (there are several delays so this may take up to 6-12 months)
* The mediator said this may be read on papers due to the small amount claimed. 

I asked the mediator, given that there is no claim and the claimant has failed to specify what he is claiming for in the particulars of claim and quantified losses, how this is still progressing through the courts. I also highlighted his failure to adhere to the Pre Action Protocol and CPR, I asked as the claim has no merits how is it still proceeding and can we request this is striked out. The mediator said we can make an application to strike out the claim, he informed me that the fee is around £250 (he highlighted this is more than what the claimant is seeking). The mediator said he is unable to give legal advice as he is not legally trained. 

The mediator said he would advise continuing to communicate and coming to an agreement with the claimant until the court date. He suggested someone else communicate with him (given his emails to me). 

The mediation is confidential so will not be shared with the court, the court will only be informed that mediation was unsuccessful.

{noformat}WITH demands_agg AS (
SELECT
  http://doo.id                                    AS order_id,
  doo.created                                 AS order_created,
  DATE_TRUNC('day', doo.created)              AS order_created_day,
      doub.city_id                                AS city_id,
      CASE
      WHEN price_before_discount IS NULL OR campaign_applied IS NULL THEN doo.delivery_price
              ELSE doc.price_before_discount END  AS delivery_price_before_discount,
      doo.delivery_price                          AS delivery_price_after_discount
FROM
      ng_delivery_spark.delivery_order_order doo
      LEFT JOIN (
      SELECT id, order_id, city_id
      FROM ng_delivery_spark.delivery_order_user_basket
      )                                                     doub
      ON http://doo.id  = doub.order_id
      LEFT JOIN (
      SELECT
              id,
              city_id,
              state,
              order_user_basket_id,
              price_before_discount,
              price_after_discount
      FROM
              ng_delivery_spark.delivery_order_campaign
      WHERE
              target = 'delivery_price' AND
              price_before_discount IS NOT NULL
      )                                                     doc
      ON doub.id = doc.order_user_basket_id
      LEFT JOIN (SELECT distinct master_basket_id, state, TRUE as campaign_applied
              FROM ng_delivery_spark.delivery_eater_campaign_code_use
                    WHERE state = 'consumed') as cu
                                          ON doo.master_basket_id = cu.master_basket_id
      WHERE DATE_TRUNC('day', doo.created) = '2023-06-01'
)
select
city_id,
SUM(delivery_price_before_discount) AS delivery_price_before_discount
FROM demands_agg
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1{noformat}

Hi [~accountid:621c92ba4160640069c52776] - a quick interim update on this as I need to sync with the regulatory team re: our global reclassification guidance for comms.

The general concerns from the legal end on comms like this are two fold:

* anything we will be saying to passengers must be 100% truthful and accurate. If we cannot verify it's accuracy, or we doubt that anything is accurate, then it should come out.
* Unless it’s absolutely critical, we do not want to say anything that may cause us issues from the reclassification side.

Some specific pointers on this:

(1) There is some interim [guidance|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONTENT/pages/4468998200/Reclassification+Risk+Copy+Guide+WIP] here on phrases that need to be avoided from the reclassification side, the one that comes up in the draft document is ‘training’, which is a word we should be avoiding.

(2) It is not yet dealt with in the guidance, but we need to be mindful of suggesting that we impose behavioural standards on drivers - for example, ‘cars must be clean' is understandable from a passenger facing perspective but it isn’t something that we actively monitor in many markets and if we DID, it would be controlling drivers in a way that is unhelpful for reclassification purposes. We should generally not be controlling the presentation of drivers in reclassification sensitive markets. I need to sync with the owner of the guidance page on this. 

(3) There is a promise in this blog that we are always checking vehicle and driver requirements. The extent that we do this varies per market. Again, we should avoid over promising.

As mentioned, I need to sync with the owner of the guidance page re: the ‘driver behaviour’ part, but those principles should guide generally on the content of these comms (and others).

I will reach out to Pedro and James on this and will update in due course. Thanks.

Hey [~accountid:6012ba2fa7fb40006901c930] ! 👋 I’ve discussed the GPS spoofing issue with the Fraud team. I’ll summarize the key points:

* *Case visibility for the Fraud team:*
** For the Fraud team, it is important that CS agents leave a comment on the order page when a rider reports an overcharge, especially for cash trips. This gives the team sufficient visibility on the volumes of such cases and case examples that may help create new prevention mechanisms for overcharges due to GPS spoofing.
* *Reacting to and preventing GPS spoofing cases:*
** Drivers find new ways of GPS spoofing, Fraud team can’t prevent all such cases. However, there are a few options still:
*** Provide CS with instructions on how to recognise GPS spoofing and what to do if it’s discovered (I’ll work on that);
*** The Product and Engineering teams have a tech solution for preventing a second device login on an active trip, which could help reduce such cases and the associated losses. This is currently being tested in some markets, there aren’t plans to roll it out globally - new releases are based on market demands. If you feel that your market would benefit from this solution, I recommend contacting Anton Grunichev to coordinate this further. 
* *About refunds:*
** We need to refund the rider the overcharge amount
** We shouldn’t ask the driver to refund the rider - a better solution would be to deduct the overcharge amount from the driver’s earnings
* *Instructions for CS to recognise GPS spoofing -* based on what I discussed with the Fraud team and your slides, these seem to be the indicators that tell the CS agent that the overcharge is caused by GPS spoofing ([~accountid:5dcebc6199e7ea0c60b0f56c][~accountid:6012ba2fa7fb40006901c930]  feel free to add any other indicators that CS should check in case something is missing):
** The estimated distance and actual driven distance don’t match (the difference is above 20 km)
** The destination entered and ride finish locations are different
** It’s a short trip and the overcharge is drastic
** In the _Route points_ tab on the order in Admin, the _“isSpeedDeltaTooFast”_ and “_isDistanceDeltaTooBig”_ signify an illogical speed calculation

* [~accountid:6012ba2fa7fb40006901c930] [~accountid:5dcebc6199e7ea0c60b0f56c] Confirm whether the CS instructions for recognising GPS spoofing are complete

The advise to the local team is to align with the POPIAs Direct Marketing requirements which are as follows:

In South Africa, the processing of personal information for the purpose of direct marketing by electronic communication is prohibited unless the data subject has given their consent. There is a limited exception for customers of the responsible party, who may be contacted for direct marketing purposes if they have been given a reasonable opportunity to object.

* *Consent*

A data subject can give their consent to direct marketing in writing, orally, or by clicking an "opt-in" checkbox. The consent must be specific and informed, and the data subject must be given the opportunity to withdraw their consent at any time.

* *Customers*

A responsible party may contact a customer for direct marketing purposes if they have obtained the customer's contact details in the context of the sale of a product or service. The customer must have been given a reasonable opportunity to object to such use of their electronic details, and they must have the right to withdraw their consent at any time.

* *Communication*

Any communication for the purpose of direct marketing must contain the following information:

# The identity of the sender or the person on whose behalf the communication has been sent. 
# An address or other contact details to which the recipient may send a request that such communications cease.

After analyzing the dependancies of the business processes (ETLs, profilings and partner payouts), we see that currently the commerce ETL is run at 3AM UTC (6AM EE time), but payments ETL is run at 5AM (8AM EE time). If we want to be dependant on the payments ETL and have fresh data, then payments ETL should be brought back to start way earlier. But it can only be moved to start at 4AM the earliest, and it runs for 1h usually (rarely also 2h) which means we would need to start our commerce ETL at 5-6AM, which is already 2-3 hours later than right now. The commerce ETL *might* run faster due to the update, and overall delay in other processes is not too bad, but this is unclear right now. Currently the commerce ETL usually runs for 1h (rarely 2-3h). So it will end  at 6-7AM.

This seems to be too big delay in the commerce ETL ending time (from ~4-5AM to ~6-7AM). The chain of business dependency that will be affected is this: *Commerce_etl → profilings → fraud calculations → partner payouts*. So the negative effect is that the partner payouts need to be moved later as well by a few hours. This means drivers will get paid later on Mondays, which can cause actual problems to them if they expect/need the payments as early as possible.



Based on these findings, we just had a talk with [~accountid:5a20f9eb748e770ed11fa3c4] [~accountid:5b7bea06cd0cc72a612c975f] and the common ground was that we will probably not start to build the dependancy on the payments ETL right now. *So overall this part of the task is postponed* *at least until* [~accountid:557058:8763ad19-5ae2-4892-91b3-a786c4dc9160] *is back from vacation.*

(-) Additional reasons to not be dependant on the payments ETL:

# Value gained from moving the commerce orders ETL to start after payments_ETL is unclear as of now, and it will be a complex thing to do since we would need to move around other processes as well. 
# It might happen that something breaks in the payments ETL and then our hands are tied as well, because we need the payments' team approval to fix it (and they may have some other higher priorities on their table at the same time). 
# Ownership of the payments data shifts away from Fraud team (maybe this is actually a positive thing?), which could cause some knowledge gaps in the Fraud team (🤔 actually this could happen right now as well..)
# As mentioned, so many other parts of the business processes depend on the commerce ETL, so it can grow into a huge project that also needs some developer hours as well, and currently the value gain from moving the schedules of all of the processes is unclear. From discussion with [~accountid:60bd1ba000bdd900683be5c4] our initial estimation was that around 3 days of developer work could be needed.

(+) Currently known reasons why it would be good to depend on the payments ETL:

# If something in business side of payments change, then the payments team will change it themselves (less maintenance for Fraud team)
# Commerce ETL runs faster (hopefully) and server costs will go down (not clear by how much)

*From my perspective, if we want to share this data with a 3rd party, we need consents of couriers since:*
1. Our Privacy Policy does not explicitly state that we can process this set of data for another purpose for which it was initially collected.
2. Given that this data has already been generated, it’s  considered as a repurposing. Hence, it limits our legal bases to three possible, and the only one that works for us is a consent to share this data for alternative purposes.
3. Fleet, as an entity, is unable to provide consent for sharing couriers' data with third parties on their behalf. Only the individuals themselves can authorize any processing activities related to their personal data.
4. Opting out refers to the opportunity to stop the data processing. Therefore, we must guarantee that couriers can request to stop processing at any time (withdraw their consent), after which we will cease processing their data.

Hey Paul,

The rationale behind is that if we share couriers' data, we need to have a legal basis to share the data with Collective Benefits (in this case it is the consent of couriers to Bolt to share date for this purpose). When Fleets provide couriers' data to us during the onboarding, they also need to have a legal ground to share it with us (it’s their responsibility to ensure they have it sharing the data with us). Bolt and Fleets are independent data controllers, so Fleets cannot manage how we process couriers' data for our purposes and vice-versa.

*In terms of reclassification risk:* in this case it does not give rise to the reclassification, since it’s the requirement of the privacy law that ONLY individual themselves can manage or authorise processing of their data. Third parties can act on behalf of the individual only if they have a power of attorney or other proof of authority. Employers are not in this list.

If the trader holds such a licence, it may carry out also the distribution of non-prescription medicines via a website.

*1.Is distance selling of medicines allowed where Bolt acts as a mediator/platform?*
Theoretically, it is permissible if: 

* the company is merely the technical provider of the website , while the actual seller of the medicinal product in invoices and delivery receipts remains the pharmacy
* the company only ensures the flow of information between the customer and the website of the Internet pharmacy concerned when supplying the medicinal product.

Such a company have to be registered in the Latvian register of postal services. The service must be available to any person with access to the internet, not only smartphone users. 

*2. Does Bolt need a licence?*
The company does not need a specific licence.

*3. Does Bolt need to check whether sellers registered on the Bolt Food platform (shops/pharmacies) have licenses to sell medical products remotely?*
The company should check whether the partner has the right to distribute OTC medicines via the website.

 OTC medicines cannot be distributed in combination with other products. Regulatory framework requires that all information on the purchase of medicinal products is separately structured and completely separate from any other products or services. Consequently, the medicines cannot be included on the company's platform as separate products alongside other products.
The advertising of medicinal products in Latvia is substantially restricted. 

*4.Is Bolt obliged to control the sale of prohibited products on the Bolt app?*
The distribution of prohibited goods is prohibited. The distribution of medicinal products without a licence is an administrative offence and the distribution of counterfeit medicinal products may, depending on the consequences, even lead to criminal prosecution.

*5.Do we need to provide any special information in the Bolt app?*
All the information required by the legislation on the requirements for a general pharmacy website in relation to the distribution of OTC medicines must be available 1:1 on any platform. Any additional explanatory note that may help consumers is welcome.

*6.Do suppliers (couriers) of medicines need medical training? Are they obliged to provide instructions on the use of medicines at the time of handover to the consumer?*
The courier is not required to have medical or pharmaceutical training, nor to be familiar with the instructions for use of the medicinal product, but must ensure that the temperature regime for the storage/transport of the medicinal product is maintained at the time of delivery, in accordance with the pharmacy's instructions.

*7.Do the answers to the above questions differ depending on whether prescription or OTC medicines are sold remotely via the platform?*
The sale of prescription-only medicines via a website is prohibited.

+*AB RESEARCH*+

Class E is a new Use Class (Commercial, Business and Service), introduced on 1st September 2020, includes a broad and diverse range of uses which principally serve the needs of visiting members of the public and or are suitable for a town centre area.

*New Class E uses benefit from permitted development rights that include:* 

* Changes to use class C3 (dwellinghouses) subject to prior approval
* Changes to a mixed use for anything within Class E and as up to two flats subject to prior approval and back again
* Change to a state funded school or back to a previous lawful use

+*INFORMATION ON SUI GENERIS*+

* Use class Sui Generis of the [Use Classes Order 1987|http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1987/764/contents/made] (as amended) are all other locations which do not fit into one of the other categories, they are unique in themselves.
* Sui Generis – Properties not fitting in any of the above categories / use classes. Meaning “of its (his, her, or their) own kind; in a class by itself; unique” 

+*Sui Generis Examples*+

_The list below is not a complete list_

theatres
betting offices
payday loan shops
funfairs
large houses in multiple occupation (seven or more)
‘Alkali work’ (any work registrable under the [Alkali, etc. Works Regulation Act 1906|https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/Edw7/6/14/contents] (as amended)) 
hostels providing no significant element of care 
scrap yards
yard for the storage/distribution of minerals
yard for the breaking of motor vehicles
fuel stations
locations selling and / or displaying motor vehicles
retail warehouse clubs
nightclubs
launderettes
police stations 
taxi businesses
car hire locations
amusement arcades and centres
casinos
landfill sites
motorsport arenas
firearm range
postal sorting offices
public house, wine bar or drinking establishment
drinking establishment with expanded food provision
hot food takeaway where consumption is mainly away from the location of purchase
venue for live music performance
cinema
concert hall
bingo hall
dance hall

+*Implications of Sui Generis Use Class*+

* As a use class, Sui Generis properties do not automatically benefit from the permitted development rights to change to an alternative use. This is to say, a change of use from a Sui Generis use or to a Sui Generis will often be subject to full local consideration through the planning application process.
* Even to change from one Sui Generis use to another Sui Generis use often requires planning permission. Certain sources indicated that permission is only required if the Sui Generis use is materially different from the existing use. 

+*Sui Generis and Planning Permission*+

* The different use classes are set out in the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987. This stipulates that in terms of planning permission, if a use of land is to change within a use class, then this does not require planning permission. However, planning permission is usually needed where the change of use involves activities within the sui generis category. These include theatres, petrol filling stations, casinos, amusement centres, car hire businesses, and so on. See Sui generis for more information.
* There are, however, permitted development rights that allow movement between some sui generis uses and other uses. There is a common misconception that changing the use from an existing use class to a sui generis class always requires planning permission. Permission is only required if the sui generis use is materially different from the existing one.
* If there is any doubt, a lawful development certificate can be applied for. This must include a detailed and unambiguous description of the use, operations or other matter for which it is to be granted. The characteristics of the matter should be spelled out in detail to avoid future problems of interpretation.

It may be that these particular Licensors are not informed on how Bolt operates as a business, they may think that Bolt is like the ‘typical’ Taxi Business (with someone taking bookings at as desk in an office with a fleet of cars outside) this may be why they push back on Use Class e(g)(i). I would suggest liaising with the Licensors that are requesting Sui Generis to try and explain to them that Bolt runs its administrative operations from the offices however the activity takes place elsewhere (given that this is a ride hailing app and differentiates from the ‘normal’ Taxi Business).

--

“*In addition to the general copyright and licence policy applicable to the whole Eurostat website, the following specific provisions apply to the datasets you are downloading.* The download and usage of these data is subject to the acceptance of the following clauses:

# The Commission agrees to grant the non-exclusive and not transferable right to use and process the Eurostat/GISCO geographical data downloaded from this page (the "data").
 
# The permission to use the data is granted on condition that:
 
## *the data will not be used for commercial purposes;*
## the source will be acknowledged. A copyright notice, as specified below, will have to be visible on any printed or electronic publication using the data downloaded from this page.

--

One option is to contact the EU Publications Office, explain the intended use and ask if such use requires their license or not. According to their website any question regarding the copyright or re-use of Eurostat data or texts may be sought from the Publications Office of the European Union at the following address:

Publications Office,
Copyright and Legal Issues
2, rue Mercier, 2985 Luxembourg

DLA Indicative timeline of the next steps in the liquidation process: 

----

Hi Michelle

Regarding Taxify Oy’s liquidation process, we’ve submitted the Trade Register notification regarding the commencement of the liquidation process, appointment of the liquidator and applied for the public summons to the creditors of the company. We assessed the matter upon contact from Mr. Zweigbergk’s attorney and concluded that Mr. Zweigbergk’s objections did not prevent the AGM meeting from being held and the AGM resolving on the liquidation. We will also send the AGM minutes to Mr. Zweigbergk and inform him briefly about the process.

Next up in the process:

 

|*#*|*Step*|*Estimated time / date*|*Status*|
|#|We will wait for the FPRO (Finnish authority) to register the commencement of the liquidation and for the public summons to creditors to be registered and published in the Official Journal of the FPRO. In the public summons, the company’s creditors are asked to notify the FPRO about their receivables from the company no later than on the due date as provided by the FPRO in the summons. The due date shall be at the earliest 3 months from the date on which the FPRO publishes the public notice about the summons.|Week 32 (7-11 August)|FPRO handling pending|
|#|After the FPRO has registered the public summons and published the due date, the liquidator will inform the company’s known creditors at least 1 month before the due date of the public summons and about the list of creditors.|Week 40 (2-6 October)|-|
|#|Due date for the company’s creditors to notify the FPRO about their receivables from the company. After the due date, the FPRO will inform the liquidator about whether any creditors have notified their receivables.
 
Once the due date of the public summons has passed and all known debts of the company have been paid, the liquidator shall distribute possible remaining assets of the company. If a debt is disputed, not yet due or otherwise not repayable, the necessary funds shall be set aside, and the remainder distributed. In case the debts of the company exceed its assets, the liquidator shall file for bankruptcy.|Week 45 (6-10 November)|-|
|#|We will prepare the liquidator’s report of the administration of the liquidation process (so called ‘final settlement’) which shall include the financial statements from the liquidation period.|Week 46 (13-17 November)|-|
|#|The liquidator shall without undue delay convene a general meeting for the shareholders to approve the final settlement (notice to be sent to the shareholders at least 1 week prior to the general meeting). When the final settlement is approved, by which the liquidation ends.
 
The company is deemed to have been dissolved once the liquidator have presented the final settlement to the general meeting.|Week 47 (20-24 November)|-|
|#|The liquidator shall without delay notify the dissolution for registration.|Week 47-48 (27 November – 1 December)|-|

 The above timetable is indicative and as such, subject to change (it’s difficult to estimate the exact handling times with the FPRO partly due to the ongoing vacation period). However, it reflects the main steps of the process and an approximate timeline.

To explain it in the simplest way, the position is considered headcount, and Job Requisition means that the position is ready to be inhabited.


In the ideal world, the recruitment process should start with Job Requisition as it is the sign for Recruiter to start looking for candidates (we have automated notification in one slack channel for recruiters so they know immediately when a job req is being created).
What’s the value of the position alone? It’s for the purpose of planning the hires in advance, you can have 3 positions budgeted already, but you will plan to hire in 6 months for instance. 

If you are creating a job req for an existing position it is considered a “Backfill” and the approval process for that is shorter (2 people). If you create a position and a job req and the same time, this is considered a “NEW” role which will result in a longer approval process (3 people).

Also important information, the position is always overwritten by Job Requisition. That means we always consider a job req as a main source of information.

I hope that answers your question, if something is still unclear please let me know.

The Swedish text reads as follows: “_Ett kreditinstitut är skyldigt att lämna ut uppgifter om enskildas förhållanden till institutet, om det under en utredning enligt bestämmelserna om förundersökning i brottmål begärs av undersökningsledaren eller om det begärs av åklagare i ett ärende om rättslig hjälp i brottmål, på framställning av en annan stat eller en mellanfolklig domstol, eller i ett ärende om erkännande och verkställighet av en europeisk utredningsorder Uppgifterna ska lämnas ut utan dröjsmål och i elektronisk form_”_._ 

This translates to the following: “_A credit institution is obliged to disclose information about individuals' relationships to the institution, if it is_ +_requested by the investigator during an investigation according to the provisions on preliminary investigation in criminal cases_+ _or if it is requested by prosecutors in a case of legal aid in criminal cases, at the request of another state or an international court, or in a case concerning the recognition and enforcement of a European Investigation Order. The information must be provided without delay and in electronic form_.” 

*Essentially this means that any credit institution is obliged to provide information if it is requested by the police in. preliminary investigation in criminal cases.* 

However, the question here would be if Bolt is such a credit institution or if the police need to refer to another paragraph to establish a legal basis. The credit institution in the definition of the referenced act is a +bank or credit market company+. 

Let me know if you need any further information. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

    COUNT(CASE WHEN dtv.detection_type = 'turn_restriction' AND trf.field_value = 'incorrect' THEN 1 END) AS Incorrect_TR,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN dtv.detection_type = 'turn_restriction' AND trf.field_value = 'already done' THEN 1 END) AS Already_done_TR,

  INNER JOIN ng_public.map_task_resolution_type_field rtf

  INNER JOIN ng_public.map_task_map_production_task mpt

                                 AND tr_sub.sequence_id = tr.sequence_id)
  and mdsd.created_at = (SELECT MAX(mdsd_sub.created_at)
                               FROM ng_public.map_detection_store_detection mdsd_sub
                               WHERE mdsd_sub.dedup_id = mdsd.dedup_id)
  and mdsd.id = (SELECT MAX(mdsd_subb.id)
                               FROM ng_public.map_detection_store_detection mdsd_subb
                               WHERE mdsd_subb.dedup_id = mdsd.dedup_id)
  AND rtf.field_name = 'verdict'
group by mdsd.region_id, ascode.name, mdsd.city_id, ascity.name, tr.created_by
order by region_id, city_id, Ops{code}

Investigation:
[https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/audit-log/audit-logs/view/2214062822|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/audit-log/audit-logs/view/2214062822]
Car application was created through Driver Portal *Add new vehicle* flow with _external_id_  for [https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/3864747|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/3864747] driver, but _first_name_ and _last_name_ don’t match (expected *Sabelo Dlamini*, actual [+Sifiso Mdalane+|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/2196821])

We don’t modify anyhow _first_name_ and _last_name_ on the backend, it is passed from DP and used/logged as is.

Values for _first_name_ and _last_name_ on the DP side are taken from the response of {{/driverPortal/getProfile}} endpoint, which gets it from the fleet’s {{/internal/driverPortal/getShortProfile}} endpoint (_driver_root_ table)

Can’t find the root cause of the bug, but I have suspicion on this event - [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/audit-log/audit-logs/view/2213252248|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/audit-log/audit-logs/view/2213252248]  - waiting for the answer from fleet team [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02H52XUKPG/p1688992830252439|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02H52XUKPG/p1688992830252439|smart-link] 

After further investigation, I figured out that it is not possible to change the driver_root for the driver (driver_root is used as a source for _first_name_ and _last_name_ values) - [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02H52XUKPG/p1689070758214209|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02H52XUKPG/p1689070758214209|smart-link] 
As a result, the only place we can have a bug is a frontend, where it calls{{/driverPortal/getProfile}} endpoint to get _first_name_ and _last_name_ values and pass them to {{/driverPortal/v2/addCarApplication}} endpoint - but I couldn’t reproduce it, because whenever we switch driver account, the refresh token is cleared out from the local storage (it is used for generation of accessToken which contains driver_id in it’s payload).

I am out of ideas where we have a bug, so I put it on hold.

Hey [~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0], as a general answer, entry into agreements via such form is possible in Ukraine. 

The detailed analysis is below:

# As a general matter, entry into contracts online would be acceptable under the current Ukrainian law. In recent years, the Ukrainian contract rules have been updated to support this. In particular, the Civil Code expressly provides that if parties enter into an agreement online it is deemed concluded in written form (Art. 639.2), allows entry into contracts by means of placing an offer online (Art. 641) which can be accepted by a counterparty. The Law “On Electronic Commerce” also contains more detailed regulation of the online execution of contracts and defines the way of their signing, including by a simple electronic signature (which is a very broad category).

The main aspect that will likely require additional thought would be the proper authentication of the signatory. The simpler it is at the stage of conclusion (e.g., no verification of a person filling in the form, just ticking the box), the less certain it may be in further practical situations. Therefore, we need to ensure that the individual who signed (by clicking “Submit”, etc.) was the authorized person. This may be mainly a matter of proving the existence of the contract in case of any litigation. 

Further, looking at this from the tax perspective, electronic documents signed by any means other than “qualified electronic signature” might potentially be questioned by the tax authorities. At the same time, for the purposes of any tax inspection agreements themselves may be less critical, while supporting documents such as services acceptance certificates, tax invoices, etc. are more likely to be scrutinized.

# Re this wording - _Upon acceptance of the General Terms by the Partner and submission of this form to Bolt, the Agreement shall become legally binding unless the Agreement is not deemed concluded as determined by Bolt in its own sole discretion (including but not limited to due to missing or invalid data)._ - this effect may be achieved, but potentially through a somewhat different legal structure. In particular, alternation of the moment of “entry into” of the contract at Bolt’s discretion is likely to be difficult, since it is an objective determination under the Ukrainian law. Depending on our internal procedures (e.g., would any partner be automatically accepted as long as they correctly fill in all the data or is there a deeper review), it might be possible to (a) change the sequence of conclusion of contracts, where Bolt is the accepting party and until proper acceptance no contract exists; or (b) let the contract be deemed concluded but include Bolt’s right to terminate at its discretion (then we may need to rephrase the wording to be accurate).

At the same time, if there is invalid data affecting the material terms of the agreement, the agreement would not be concluded. But this would be an objective determination and we would need to identify in advance all items that will be assigned “material terms” status. If that works for us, it should require a minor effort (compile the list of data and make sure that they are expressly identified as material terms). If we would like to have a _discretionary_ power to reject the agreement, we can consider the two options outlined above.

Please let me know if you have any questions re this.

{code:sql}with base as (

 	, a.support_case_id

 left join ng_customer_support.support_issue_store_support_issue as b
  		on a.issue_key = b.issue_key
 where 1=1 
 	and b.is_internal = false
 group by 3
 )
 select support_case.user_persona
    	, case when support_case.source = 'beehive_outgoing' then 'outgoing' else 'incoming' end as contact_type
    	, case when support_case.escalated_to_agent is null then 'not_escalated' else 'escalated' end as is_escalated_to_agent
    	, providers.is_bolt_market_provider
    	, base.issue_key_combined
    	, base.issue_key_count
    	, count(base.support_case_id) as case_count

  		on base.support_case_id = support_case.id
  	left join ng_delivery.delivery_order_order as delivery
  		on support_case.order_id = delivery.id
  	left join ng_delivery.etl_delivery_provider_info as providers
  		on delivery.provider_id = providers.provider_id
where support_case.created_date >= date('2023-05-01')
        and support_case.created_date <= date('2023-06-30')
        and support_case.user_persona in ('eater', 'provider', 'courier', 'market_consumer')

Hi [~accountid:63aa929a741248746bf63439], 

*Angle of employment risk*. Disabling a feature that allows drivers to earn more on the platform limits drivers’ right to access platform services and shows that the platform is monitoring drivers’ behaviour on the platform. Supervising the performance of work using electronic means is an element of employment.

* *General approach*. To avoid the employment risk, we recommend enabling the feature for +all drivers+. This option is well defendable and even strengthens our position against reclassification risks. We will be able to say that drivers who join us to deliver transportation services may choose different ways of how to provide services on our platform, meaning there is a lot of freedom for drivers as to how they choose to use our platform.
* *Approach with higher risk.* We may accept an approach with a higher risk in markets where reclassification risk aren’t considered high. To mitigate the employment risk and make the feature defensible to some extent, we could structure a Scheduled Rides feature for drivers as an incentive - meaning, if you do X, we enable for you a feature Y.
** *Metrics used for determining whether the incentive applies*. Please note that in order for the risk to be mitigated and the feature to be defensible, the metrics used as X shall not include metrics that measure drivers’ performance *before* the driver has accepted the trip (+*e.g. acceptance rate*+). The metrics used as X, however, could include metrics that measure drivers’ performance *after* the driver has accepted the trip (e.g. completed rides, experience of driving on the platform). The metrics for performance measurement after the acceptance of the trip are defensible, since in that case drivers have already committed to the passenger to deliver him/her to the requested destination. If the driver does not honor this commitment, the driver is in breach of the contract concluded between the driver and the rider.
* *Angle of transparency*. Should we opt for the second option as described above, we need to make it clear to the drivers that they have an opportunity to use Scheduled Rides, provided they fulfill certain criteria (e.g. have been driving on a platform for six months, have completed 100 trips etc). The transparency may be reflected on the copies. 

To answer your question on the acceptance rate, yes this would increase reclassification and we highly recommend to use other metrics if you want to limit the feature to certain drivers. We have already gone live with this approach in Sweden and currently testing it in Finland, I would recommend you to take inspiration from your Nordic colleagues as the reclassification risk is deemed similar in these countries. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

{code:sql}# Query for updating business company promo code state to inactive for all pending business company promo codes where promo code itself is not active anymore

UPDATE `taxify_business`.`business_company_promo_code` bcpc
    JOIN (SELECT bcpc.id
          FROM business_company_promo_code as bcpc
                   LEFT JOIN business_promo_code as bpc on bpc.id = bcpc.promo_code_id
          WHERE bcpc.state = 'pending'
            AND bpc.state = 'hidden') bcpc2
    ON bcpc.id = bcpc2.id
SET bcpc.state = 'inactive';{code}




{code:sql}# Query for updating business company promo code state to inactive for all pending business company promo codes where promo code itself is active and company is active as well

UPDATE `taxify_business`.`business_company_promo_code` bcpc
    JOIN (SELECT bcpc.id
          FROM business_company_promo_code AS bcpc
                   LEFT JOIN business_promo_code bpc ON bcpc.promo_code_id = bpc.id
                   LEFT JOIN business_company bc on bcpc.business_company_id = bc.id
                   LEFT JOIN business_company_price_customisation b on bc.id = b.business_company_id
          WHERE bcpc.state = 'pending'
            AND bc.state = 'active'
            AND bpc.state = 'active') bcpc2
    ON bcpc.id = bcpc2.id
SET bcpc.state = 'inactive';{code}

Hi [~accountid:62a3287576c0360069f59b72],

The first time I heard about this case was when we received the lawsuit against the insurer and Bolt. Prior to that, we received *no* pre-litigation letter to which we could respond denying our liability and refusing to compensate.

After we were notified of the lawsuit, the insurer's lawyer contacted us and proposed to represent the insurer and Bolt in this matter and to answer the lawsuit on behalf of both of them denying liability. Due to the low value and risk of the claim, Paul, Santiago (former CM) and Philip agreed to be defended by the insurance lawyer, who would not charge us a fee.

Nb: In the Spanish judicial system, once a lawsuit has been received, the next step is for the defendant to file a reply to the Court defending his position and proposing means of proof. Once the answer to the lawsuit has been produced, the hearing takes place (normally months or years after the reply). Before the hearing, the parties can reach out-of-court settlements, or the plaintiff can withdraw from the lawsuit.

Both the insurance lawyer and we wanted to go to court to defend our position, as we consider that we have no liability in this matter.

Last week, the insurance lawyer contacted us to inform us of the date of the hearing (18 March 2024 at 11.00 a.m.) and to ask if we were willing to settle out of court, meaning that Bolt would pay a compensation of 100 euros. The lawyer said that due to the low value of this litigation, it may not be worth going to court. Please note that if we lose, we will have to pay the compensation plus court costs. Even if we win, the judge will probably impose the costs ex officio, which means that each party pays its own costs.



Regarding your question about the ramifications for us in the future and whether this would set a precedent for future incidents, please note that we must differentiate between i) the consequences of this specific case and ii) the consequences for future incidents:

i) If we reach a settlement agreement, this agreement will be contractually effective, so we will be bound by it and, once approved by the court, it will be enforceable, which means that we will not be able to terminate it and go to court, but we will have to comply with it.

ii) I believe, settling this case will not set a precedent for future incidents. The so-called doctrine of actos propios would not apply to future cases, which means that if we agree to compensate the claimant in this case, we will not be obliged to compensate in similar cases in the future. The principle that no one can go against his own acts only applies when someone does something which is contrary to acts done by the same person previously and which have created a legal relationship or situation that could not be unilaterally altered by the person who was bound to respect it, for example: a father who voluntarily acknowledges  a person as a child, and subsequently intends to contest this civil status; the one who alleges the nullity of the contract and at the same time seeks, in parallel proceedings, the enforced performance of the contract, etc. For clarity, this doctrine would apply in case i) if we reach a settlement agreement and then seek to rescind the agreement and go to court to avoid paying any compensation.

# it is generally accepted that the proposal of having Partners fill in a form and accept the General Terms (whereafter the General Terms are emailed to the Partner) +*can form a valid contract in our law*+. However, please note the following:

 

# In our view this proposed wording would not be enforceable: _Upon acceptance of the General Terms by the Partner and submission of this form to Bolt, the Agreement shall become legally binding unless the Agreement_ +_is not deemed concluded as determined by Bolt in its own sole discretion (including but not limited to due to missing or invalid data)_+_._ The wording should rather state: “_Upon acceptance of the General Terms by the Partner and proper completion of this form to Bolt (without any missing or invalid data) the Agreement shall become legally binding._” If there is proper acceptance of the offer, a contract has been entered into and Bolt cannot unilaterally determine that one has not been entered into.
# We suggest that a click-wrap agreement is used whereby the Partner is required to click on the terms and click “I hereby agree to these terms and conditions” at the bottom thereof. This ensures that the Partner was aware of the terms and actively accepted them – which provides evidence that the Partner agreed to be bound thereto.
# Further, the Consumer Protection Act provides that certain categories of clauses which could be seen as prejudicial (i.e. clauses which limit the risk or liability of the supplier or any other person; clauses which constitute an assumption of risk or liability by the consumer; clauses which impose an obligation on the consumer to indemnify the supplier or any other person for any cause; or clauses which purport to be an acknowledgment of any fact by a consumer) should be pointed out to the consumer. When such a term is pointed out, the nature and potential effect of the clause should be explained and a consumer should be given adequate opportunity to receive and comprehend the provision. If these requirements are not met, Bolt will not be able to rely on the restriction. For example, if there is a limitation of liability clause in respect of the restaurant, it will not apply and the restaurant will have its usual full claim (based on normal legal and common law principles) against Bolt, without the restriction. *Recommendation: We should highlight in bold clauses were our liability is limited and include this disclaimer:* +*_PLEASE PAY PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO THE CLAUSES IN BOLD AS THESE CLAUSES EITHER SEEK TO LIMIT OUR OR ANY OTHER PERSON’S RISK OR LIABILITY, CONSTITUTE AN ASSUMPTION OF RISK OR LIABILITY BY YOU, IMPOSE ANY OBLIGATION ON YOU TO INDEMNIFY US OR ANY OTHER PERSON, OR PURPORT TO BE AN ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF ANY FACT BY YOU._*+

sure, I can give you some examples, but I have right now not for every EC an example Beehive case or tool ready. If you need them, then I will try to find them and add them later to this ticket.

 *Unsafe Parking:*

The SOP requires an investigative block, but in most cases the user parked the rental vehicle hours or even days before the actual event.

Example ticket/order/tool: [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/242335376|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/242335376]
[https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/rentals-micromobility/orders/edit/germany/90833824?tab=details|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/rentals-micromobility/orders/edit/germany/90833824?tab=details]
Tool Ref# S-395666

The user got blocked by SME by on the SOP despite the scooter getting parked *before* the car of the reporting third party was parked.
SME then asked us in Slack whether they can unblock the user or not. To see [the question|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05ETCVK9KL/p1688722008136459] of SME, I would need to add you the private majorel-mm-hp channel. 

*User and Cyclist Incident*

The SOP requires an investigative block, but in many cases the user reports the incident themselves to us, especially if the rental vehicle was faulty, leading to the accident or if the fault is not clear.

Example ticket/order/tool:

[https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/243680876|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/243680876]
[https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/rentals/orders/edit/germany/91317412|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/rentals/orders/edit/germany/91317412]
Tool Ref# S-399000

User reports that due to bad brakes they collided with a cyclist.
According to the SOP, SME blocked the user as the accused party, even though the user reported the case to us and blames faulty equipment as the cause of the accident.
SME [asked|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05ETCVK9KL/p1689003128465429?thread_ts=1689000703.016099&cid=C05ETCVK9KL] then in Slack majorel-mm-hp if they should inform the user about the block or not. I advised them to remove the block.
This case is actually the case prompting this SD-ticket.



The same logic for User and Cyclist Incident should apply also to the other ECs in my list. Whenever a user reports an incident and accuses themselves directly or indirectly of being at fault for these EC, then we should, most of the time, not block for the investigation, but rather at the end of the investigation as a consequence based on the determined Root Cause Incident.
This argument is similar to our discussion in [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/RS-451|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/RS-451|smart-link] about when we consider a user to be at fault for a personal accident.

If a user reports that they collided with a vehicle because they drove through a pothole, misjudged the road conditions, then the SOP requires an investigative block. The Root Cause then determines if the user is at fault per default or not.

In the past, we never blocked users for self-reported accidents inline with Local OPS in order to encourage the report of such incidents. We always feared that blocking users in such situations will lead to fewer reports and negative user experience because they get punished for contacting us.
